newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IMF ready to sign new accord with Argentina - paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF ready to sign new accord with Argentina - paper.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is prepared to sign a new extended fund facility with Argentina in 1998, La Nacion newspaper Monday quoted a senior IMF official as saying.
"Argentina has met its policy commitments and we have continued to support the structural reforms," Claudio Loser, IMF director for the western hemisphere, told La Nacion.
"We think that the elements are there for a favorable negotiation for an extended fund facility when the current program ends," he added.

Argentina has a stand-by loan agreement with the IMF that expires at the end of this year. Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez has said he hopes to establish an agreement with the fund that extends until 2000.
Negotiations for the new agreement will start in April.
Loser, who noted that Argentina's economic stability has consolidated in recent months, said he was confident Argentina is improving its fiscal situation.
"We see a clear profile for a reduction in the deficit," said the official.
In 1996, Argentina had a deficit of $6.0 billion and it expects to reduce that to $4.5 billion this year and to $1.5 in 1998.
